transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-09 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Recording: yes (auto)
- Notes: discovery / security intake

Summary (auto):
Redwood AE + SE introduced platform options and controls. BlueLoom described production constraints: PII-ish logs, EU data residency, and need for strict KMS control. Discussed SOC2/ISO posture and SSO requirements, retention windows, and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I know we have about an hour, I'll kick off real quick; Ethan from our SE team is here to go deeper on the architecture and the KMS question.
[00:08] Daniel (BlueLoom): Great thanks Maya. I'm Daniel, CTO. Sofia and Priya are here from platform and security. We're primarily evaluating options for inference hosting — latency matters for customer-facing features, but we also have strict compliance needs.
[00:20] Sofia (BlueLoom): Yeah hi. We run a global product, EU users are big for us, and there are two classes of data: public prompts and user-uploaded docs that are regulated.
[00:32] Priya (BlueLoom): Quick intro — I'm Priya, I own security for platform. High level: we need SOC2 Type II, ideally ISO 27001, SSO via SAML + SCIM for provisioning, RBAC mapped to AD groups, audit logs retained for 12 months, and HSM-backed KMS for keys. Also interested in data deletion guarantees.
[00:54] Maya: That's super helpful, thanks. Quick high-level on Redwood: we offer Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments (VPC or on-prem). Hosted is quickest; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and data isolation on a tenant level; Private gives you a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem. Ethan, do you want to add the KMS/HSM part?
[01:12] Ethan (Redwood): Sure — we support several key flows. For Hosted we do BYOK via a customer-managed KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and have HSM options for enterprise contracts). For Dedicated, we can do tenant-level encryption keys and limited key cust, and for Private you control the KMS entirely in your VPC, we can integrate with your HSM. There are some nuances around logging and telemetry that change a bit by deployment model.
[01:37] Priya: When you say BYOK for Hosted — do you mean we hand a key and you wrap it, or you never see plaintext? We need proof that customer keys are strictly under our control and that Redwood can't decrypt model payloads in transit or at rest.
[01:49] Ethan: Right — good callout. For Hosted BYOK we use envelope encryption; customer master key (CMK) in your cloud KMS wraps data keys. Redwood's serving nodes see only the data key encrypted; we don't have access to the CMK. Operationally we do need to cache the data key in memory for serving; for ultra-sensitive use you should consider Private where the KMS is entirely under your network boundary.
[02:12] Daniel: That memory cache — is that encrypted or protected by an HSM? If an attacker got host access it's concerning.
[02:18] Ethan: The in-memory KV/cache is protected by the node's OS and runtime protections; we can enable process isolation and restrict debug access. With Private deployments, you can enforce strict host hardening and HSM-backed keys with no external access. We can provide detailed hardened node configs.
[02:36] Sofia: Okay. On SSO side, we use Okta and SCIM for groups — group-based RBAC is critical. Can Redwood sync groups over SCIM and honor AD group mappings for role bindings?
[02:47] Maya: Yes, we have SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. We map SCIM groups to roles in the Console; you can create role bindings to match your AD groups. We also have fine-grained RBAC for APIs and Console. Ethan, anything to call out on audit logging?
[03:03] Ethan: Audit logs are available in Hosted with retention defaults; for Dedicated and Private you can route logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk or to an S3 bucket. We sign logs and produce tamper-evident sequences; retention windows are configurable. For hosted customers we retain 90 days by default, but enterprise customers can extend or export.
[03:22] Priya: We need 12 months of immutable audit logs and proof of tamper-evidence for our auditors. Do you provide logs with a SHA chain or signed buckets?
[03:30] Ethan: We can provide signed log bundles and export to your S3 with server-side encryption and bucket lock. For Private, you control the retention entirely. We'll include the log schema and examples in the artifacts we send.
[03:44] Daniel: On compliance, do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001? We require evidence.
[03:50] Maya: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and we're in progress on ISO 27001 — we have a roadmap and some cert evidence for subcomponents. I'll attach the SOC2 report and the current ISO artifacts in the follow-up.
[03:59] Priya: If ISO isn't complete we need more evidence for ISO controls — vulnerability scanning cadence, third-party assessments, and change management proof.
[04:08] Maya: Understood. I'll include the pen test cadence, vuln scanning reports abstracts, and our change management doc.
[04:15] Sofia: About data residency — EU data must stay in EU for certain user classes. Can you route regions and enforce residency per-tenant?
[04:24] Ethan: Yes — we can route by policy. Hosted can pin to a region (e.g., eu-west-1) and Dedicated pools can be regionally located. Private obviously sits in your VPC region. There's a nuance: shared hosted infra might still have control plane metadata outside region unless you do Dedicated or Private — we can show exact data flows in the architecture doc.
[04:45] Priya: Control plane telemetry — what metadata do you collect? We need clarity on PHI/PII handling.
[04:50] Maya: We collect request metadata (timestamps, model, route), but not user content unless customers opt-in for debugging. For enterprise contracts we can disable content retention and restrict telemetry. We'll include the telemetry schema.
[05:03] Daniel: Let's talk about the deployment decision. Our product needs 50–70 QPS at peak, p95 latency under 250ms for short prompts. Cost matters but stability and compliance are priority. We're leaning Dedicated for primary traffic and Private for sensitive document processing. Thoughts?
[05:21] Ethan: That's a common pattern. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and single-tenant GPU pools. Private for batch or high-security workloads is ideal. We should run a quick benchmark mapping your expected prompt lengths to model configs, quantization, and batching. That will show cost/latency curves.
[05:36] Sofia: On the audit side, if we use Dedicated and you route logs to our S3, who manages log integrity? We want an attestation model.
[05:43] Ethan: If logs are exported to your S3, you manage bucket lock and immutability. Redwood can sign logs prior to export; we can also provide a signed chain and a small verifier script.
[05:54] Priya: Deletion requests — if a user requests deletion, can you guarantee purge from backups and caches? We need a policy that aligns with GDPR erasure.
[06:03] Maya: We have deletion APIs and processes. For Hosted we provide best-effort purge and can disable retention; for Dedicated/Private you get more direct control. Backups are rotated; we can provide retention and purge timelines. For strict GDPR deletion we'd recommend Private with customer-managed storage.
[06:24] Daniel: Mentioned earlier you have intelligent batching and KV cache — how does KV cache handle PII prefixes?
[06:30] Ethan: KV cache can be scoped per-tenant and you can disable KV caching for sensitive routes. Also you can configure prefix caching policies in Redwood Optimize. We'll show config examples.
[06:42] Sofia: We also want to know about incident response and SLAs — RTO/RPO, routing for incident comms, and legal sub-processes.
[06:49] Maya: For enterprise customers we offer 99.9% uptime SLAs, on-call escalation, and an IR runbook. I'll attach the SLA and our IR contact flow.
[06:58] Priya: One last thing — do you have a bring-your-own-model option? We run some proprietary finetuned models we might want to serve behind your runtime but keep weights private.
[07:07] Ethan: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can bring your model; we support model onboarding with encrypted weights. For Hosted we generally serve curated models but can discuss partner arrangements.
[07:20] Daniel: Perfect. Sounds like next step is an SE deep dive focused on Private/VPC mapping and a short benchmark. Also we'll need SOC2 artifacts and pricing.
[07:31] Maya: Yep. I'll send the SOC2 and the security pack after this call and coordinate the deep dive slot.
[07:38] Sofia: Thanks. Also please include a sample SAML metadata config and SCIM mapping examples so our Okta team can review.
[07:46] Maya: Will do.
[07:49] Priya: Cool, thanks all.
[07:52] Ethan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

Auto-close: Meeting ended with clear next steps and assigned owners.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional ASR errors on acronyms (e.g., "KV cache" heard as "K V cash"), product names slightly garbled in places; speaker turns sometimes grouped.
